findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/prompt-contracts.ts:396-416 — MEDIUM: validatePromptEnvelope treats every optional field as merely nonblank, so digest-bearing fields such as toolPolicyDigest and systemInstructionDigest accept arbitrary strings. Runtime reproduction with toolPolicyDigest="not-a-digest" prints MALFORMED_OPTIONAL_DIGEST_ACCEPTED. This contradicts CHK-001 adversarial schema intent requiring malformed digest values to fail closed and leaves the foundational Story-2 envelope schema permissive before it becomes gate-bound. Split optional digest fields from optional text/reference fields and validate each digest with requireDigest; add mutation probes for all optional digest-bearing fields.

packages/main/src/core/prompt-contracts.ts:161-198 — MEDIUM: canonicalJsonStringify enumerates only Object.keys and therefore silently drops symbol-keyed own properties instead of rejecting non-CanonicalJson input. Runtime reproduction canonicalJsonStringify({a:1,[Symbol("hidden")]:2}) returns {"a":1}, allowing two structurally different inputs to collapse to the same canonical bytes/digest. This directly violates CHK-001 canonical-fail-closed intent that unsupported values must not disappear or produce an admissible digest. Reject own symbol keys (and cover the mutation in the focused smoke) before canonicalizing object entries.

packages/main/src/core/prompt-role-contract-registry.ts:249 The supposedly frozen lifecycle registry does not fail closed on replacement drift. validatePromptRoleContracts checks membership, the 12/3/1 partition, retired-channel/default status, and compatibility status, but never verifies the accepted exact mappings (test-intent/test-case-reviewer -> verification-intent and implementation-reviewer -> quality+behavior guidance). Reproducer against the built module: clone PROMPT_ROLE_CONTRACTS, change test-intent.replacementAgentType to lattice-review-quality, then call validatePromptRoleContracts(...); it returns successfully (ACCEPTED_INVALID_REPLACEMENT). This directly violates CHK-004's requirement that replacement metadata violating frozen policy be rejected and would let a semantically different compatibility migration target retain an admissible registry shape.

packages/main/src/core/prompt-contracts.ts:127 canonicalJsonStringify enumerates objects with Object.keys(), so unsupported own symbol keys and non-enumerable own fields silently disappear instead of failing closed. A plain object with a=1, one with an own Symbol key whose value is undefined, and one with a non-enumerable own hidden=undefined all serialize to the same {a:1} canonical JSON and produce the same domain-separated digest. That contradicts CHK-001's explicit invariant that unsupported/undefined values cannot disappear or collapse to an admissible digest, and it creates a content-address collision class before PromptEnvelope uses this primitive. Reject non-string/non-enumerable own keys (or otherwise mechanically constrain the accepted object domain) and add mutation probes.

packages/main/src/tasks/prompt-contract-measurement-smoke.ts:100-205 and 327-335 — HIGH: the focused smoke never deletes a required field from RuntimeContract, RoleContract, PromptMeasurementRecord, or PromptEnvelope. It tests unknown/invalid values, but the must adversarial intent and recorded evidence explicitly claim missing required fields fail closed. A regression that stops requiring one field could therefore pass this suite. Add representative required-key deletion probes for all four schemas (ideally table-driven) and rerun the bound evidence.

scripts/verify-proof-or-stop-prompt-baseline.mjs:2291-2409 — MEDIUM: --probe-baseline-drift mutates structuredClone(current) and compares two in-memory snapshots; it never changes one actual assembled Prompt/template, observes the normal verifier fail on bytes/hash, restores the source, and observes PASS. CHK-004 adversarial:2 requires that exact integration/restore path, while its evidence note accurately says only synthetic mutations. Add a non-destructive temp-worktree or injectable collector integration probe that exercises the real collection boundary and proves repository restoration.
